skill.description: Match short mood descriptions to visual styles and art-direction vocabulary using a cached dictionary, with optional paid cloud analysis and reference-image metadata.

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives involving Markdown backticks, Chinese documentation, ordinary indexing, and expected cache operations. Confirmed risks involve quota-token forwarding across redirects and an endpoint override that permits plaintext HTTP. No evidence found of malware, prompt injection, or unrelated credential collection.

remediation.issue: Default urllib redirect handling can forward X-FS-Quota to another host or an HTTP destination.
remediation.suggestion: Reject redirects for authenticated requests, or permit only same-origin HTTPS redirects and strip quota tokens before any origin change.

remediation.issue: FS_API_BASE accepts plaintext HTTP endpoints for requests carrying quota tokens and cloud input.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the endpoint scheme before requests and require HTTPS when transmitting credentials or input; document trust requirements for custom hosts.

content.user_title: Find Visual Styles from Mood Descriptions
content.value_statement: Mood descriptions often lack precise art-direction vocabulary. Feeling Search matches short descriptions to visual styles, definitions, and supporting words through a cached dictionary.
actual_capabilities: Match descriptions up to 500 characters against cached feeling words and rank associated visual styles.
Recognize Chinese and English style names directly in descriptions.
Expand matching through gloss synonyms while excluding the final antonym or confusable terms.
Look up word-to-style links and retrieve the words associated with a style through free API endpoints.
Use paid cloud analysis after zero local word matches when cloud access is enabled and a quota token is configured.
Retrieve paid style details and reference-image metadata for batches of up to five style identifiers.
limitations: Requires Python 3.8 or later and an initial dictionary download; offline analysis currently fails when the cache has expired.
Accepts text up to 500 characters, not images or URLs; local matching depends on dictionary coverage rather than full semantic understanding.
Cloud analysis, style details, and image retrieval require paid service access; word and style-word lookups also require network access.
Does not generate images or guarantee artistic suitability or commercial reuse rights for referenced assets.

use_cases.title: Develop a concept-art direction
use_cases.description: Translate a scene's mood into candidate visual styles and inspect the words supporting each match.

use_cases.title: Refine image-generation vocabulary
use_cases.description: Find named styles and related descriptors to incorporate into prompts for a separate image-generation tool.

use_cases.title: Compare brand visual references
use_cases.description: Explore style candidates for a brand brief and request attributed reference-image metadata only after approving paid access.

prompt_templates.title: Find initial style candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find visual styles for a rainy convenience-store entrance with cold white lighting. Use local matching only and explain each candidate's matching words.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: explore art-direction vocabulary without paid analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Expand a weak match
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this mood: [description]. Try exact matching, then free fuzzy matching if needed. Compare the results without calling paid endpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve dictionary recall while keeping cloud analysis disabled.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a style's vocabulary
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the words associated with cyberpunk through the free endpoint. Explain which words distinguish it and suggest vocabulary for my brief: [brief].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: refine a known art direction using style-specific words.

prompt_templates.title: Build an attributed shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank styles for [brief] locally first. Ask before paid cloud analysis or image retrieval. Present definitions, matched words, source labels, and available image credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine candidate ranking, consent, and reference attribution.

best_practices: Download the dictionary before offline work and use exact matching before trying fuzzy matching.
Confirm the service endpoint and obtain consent before transmitting confidential briefs or using paid operations.
Explain matched words, distinguish local and cloud results, and verify image licenses and attribution before reuse.
anti_patterns: Treating a dictionary match as the only correct artistic interpretation.
Sending confidential briefs to cloud analysis or spending quota without user approval.
Using placeholder images as style evidence or assuming every reference permits commercial reuse.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images?
faq.answer: No. It returns style candidates, vocabulary, and optional reference-image metadata for use with separate creative tools.

faq.question: Which operations are free?
faq.answer: Local matching, dictionary downloads, word lookups, style-word lookups, and status checks are free. Cloud analysis, style details, and image retrieval consume quota.

faq.question: Can I use it without an internet connection?
faq.answer: Local analysis works with a valid dictionary cache. The current implementation rejects expired caches offline; word lookups and reference retrieval require connectivity.

faq.question: When is my description sent to the cloud?
faq.answer: Cloud analysis sends it only after zero local word matches, with --allow-cloud enabled and FS_QUOTA configured. Initial dictionary downloads do not include descriptions.

faq.question: What inputs does it accept?
faq.answer: Provide a short text description of up to 500 characters. The workflow supports Chinese or English descriptions but depends on available dictionary vocabulary.

faq.question: Are reference images cleared for commercial use?
faq.answer: Do not assume clearance. Review each image's kind, credit, license, and source URL, and exclude placeholders from style evidence.
